budget_measurement.counted: output tokens of every investigation request, plus direct tool results and code execution output as Claude saw them; programmatic tool results and web search result content are not included

findings.claim: Deploy dep-8841 (09:14:00-09:14:47, all 6 checkout-api instances) changed only checkout/payment_client.py. The payment Retry went from status_forcelist {502,504}, allowed_methods {GET}, backoff 0.5 to {502,503,504}, allowed_methods None (so POST /v1/charges is retried), backoff 0. The runbook says a DB connection is held through the entire gateway call, retries included. Pool: 15 connections, pool_timeout 10s.

TRIGGER: the third-party payment gateway returned HTTP 503 (upstream capacity) on POST /v1/charges from 09:19:37.951Z to 09:21:09.037Z (138 error lines). payment_gateway_5xx_rate rose from 0 at 09:19:30 to a peak of 77.8% at 09:20:50 and was back to 0 by 09:21:40. It was 0 before that, including after the 09:14 deploy.

The new config retried gateway 503s on POST with no backoff, up to 4 attempts, while each request held its DB connection. Example trace: 4 x 503 over 31,384 ms, all with the connection held (conn_hold_ms=31384). Checkouts that eventually succeeded also held connections for 7-28s over 2-4 attempts. Normal checkout p95 was about 215 ms, and the peak was 43,875 ms.

The pool was exhausted: db_pool_in_use went from about 1 to 14 at 09:19:45 and stayed at capacity (15/15) from 09:19:55 through 09:20:50, dropping to 2 by 09:21:05. checkout_5xx_rate started rising at 09:20:05, about 10s after the pool filled, which matches pool_timeout=10s. It peaked at 61.2% at 09:20:50.

FAILURE MODE: checkout-api-3 returned 124 customer-facing 503s between 09:19:56.7Z and 09:21:04.4Z. 105 (85%) were reason=db_pool_checkout_timeout (waited_ms=10000, pool_in_use=15/15). Traces show these on GET /orders/{id} (42), POST /checkout (37), and GET /cart (26); the only span is db.acquire_connection timing out at 10s. /cart and /orders never call the gateway. Only 19 were payment_gateway_unavailable after 4 attempts. So most of the outage came from checkout-api's own pool exhaustion, which spread to endpoints that don't use the gateway, rather than from gateway errors passed straight through.

Runbook step 3 (timing): checkout-api 503s ended at 09:21:04.4Z and gateway 503s at 09:21:09.0Z, so the checkout errors did not outlast the gateway incident. The pool drained (15 to 2) at 09:21:05, and the metric's tail to 09:21:25 is just the 30s rate window rolling off. This fits amplification during the gateway burst, not a lingering fault inside checkout-api.

Host CPU saturation ruled out: cpu_percent on checkout-api-3 ranged from 25.5% to a max of 36.0% for the whole 09:13-09:24:30 window, including the outage. It never got near saturation, so it cannot explain 10s pool waits or 40s p95. The slight rise tracks the extra retry traffic.

Inventory-service warning ruled out: it is one WARN at 09:20:30Z saying SKU HC-2291 is below its reorder threshold (4 remaining). That is a business stock notice, and it arrived 50s after the gateway errors started. inventory-service had no ERROR lines (the ERRORs are only payment-gateway 138 and checkout-api 124). The stock check is async per the architecture diagram, and no failed trace contains an inventory span; the failures are db.acquire_connection timeouts or payment_gateway.charge 503s.

Web-frontend warning ruled out: it is one WARN at 09:20:10Z about a deprecated analytics snippet legacyTrack() on /checkout, which the log itself says has "No functional impact". web-frontend had no ERROR lines, and the 503s come from checkout-api server-side (pool timeouts and gateway failures), not from the frontend.

hypotheses.hypothesis: ROOT CAUSE: deploy dep-8841 set the payment client to retry 503s on POST (allowed_methods=None) with zero backoff and up to 4 attempts. Because checkout-api holds a DB connection for the whole gateway call, retries included, the brief gateway 503 burst (TRIGGER, about 09:19:38 to 09:21:09) stretched connection hold times from about 200ms to 7-31s. That drained the 15-connection pool, and requests on every endpoint then timed out after 10s waiting for a connection. FAILURE MODE: customers got 503s on /checkout, /cart and /orders/{id} (85% pool timeouts, 15% gateway-exhausted) and p95 latency up to about 44s. Before this deploy, 503s were not retried and POST was never retried, so the gateway burst would have caused fast-failing checkout errors only, with no pool exhaustion. Reverting the Retry config, or releasing the DB connection before the payment call, should prevent a repeat. Blind retries of non-idempotent charge POSTs also risk double charges.
hypotheses.supporting_evidence: Diff and runbook (S01). Gateway 503 burst (S06, S10). 4-attempt, 31s connection-holding traces (S13, S07). Pool pinned at 15/15, with checkout 5xx starting 10s later (S05, S02). 105 of 124 errors are pool timeouts, including on non-gateway endpoints (S09, S12). Errors end together with the gateway burst (S09, S10). CPU, inventory and frontend alternatives ruled out (S04, S07, S08).

hypotheses.hypothesis: Competing (weaker): the gateway outage alone explains the outage, and the retry change was incidental.
hypotheses.supporting_evidence: Gateway 5xx and checkout 5xx overlap in time (S06, S02). But only 19 of 124 checkout 503s were gateway failures. 105 were pool timeouts, including 68 on /cart and /orders, which never call the gateway (S09, S12). That damage needs the long connection hold that the new retry policy caused (S13, S01). A counterfactual replay with the old retry config should test this.

documentation.claim: urllib3 Retry: allowed_methods=None means retry on any verb (including non-idempotent POST); a status retry fires when the method is in allowed_methods and the status is in status_forcelist; backoff_factor controls sleep between attempts (0 = immediate retries).
